images.title: One diagonal of a kite cuts the other in half at 90°
images.purpose: Shows kite ABCD with AB = BC and CD = DA, whose diagonal BD cuts AC in half at right angles at O.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large kite in the centre, its equal sides marked, both diagonals drawn with a right angle mark.
images.exact_structure: One kite ABCD in dark outline: B at the top, D at the bottom, A on the left, C on the right, with BD vertical and about twice as long as AC, and O closer to B than to D. Sides AB and BC each carry one short tick mark; sides CD and DA each carry two short tick marks. The vertical diagonal BD is a thick teal (#0072B2) line and the horizontal diagonal AC a thick amber (#E69F00) line; they cross at O. A small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) square right angle mark at O. Half diagonals AO and OC each carry one small amber cross mark, showing they are equal. Two equal small reddish purple arcs at B, one each side of BD. The letters A, B, C, D sit outside their corners and O right of the crossing. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In a kite, the diagonal BD cuts AC in half at right angles.
images.description: Shows kite ABCD with AB = BC and CD = DA, whose diagonal BD cuts AC in half at right angles at O.
images.context: SSS on ∆ABD and ∆CBD, then SAS on ∆AOB and ∆COB; the two angles at O make 180°, so each is 90°.

image_decisions.why: Marking the equal sides, the halves AO = OC and the right angle shows the whole kite result in one figure.
